_comment: The pinned corpus. This file is the authoritative record of which catalog the system
was built against; PINNED.md beside it explains why the file is vendored and what is
irregular about it, and restates none of these values.
NIST publishes new releases. An unpinned catalog means the corpus can change under a
green build, and anything scored against it is then silently measuring a different
document. The hash is what makes that visible; the counts are what make a swapped
release visible even when it parses cleanly.
What the loader finds in the file above. Checked by `make catalog` and by the tests.
`live` is `base_controls + enhancements - withdrawn`, and it is the number of records
the chunker is expected to produce; `parts` counts every part at every depth.
